newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGBs seen edging higher, target 125.40.
newsitem.headline: JGBs seen edging higher, target 125.40.

text.p: The key September 10-year Japanese government bond futures contract is expected to have an upward bias on Friday, supported by market's view that interest rates are likely to remain steady for some time.
"The Bank of Japan governor's comments this week have reassured the market that monetary policy is likely to remain steady for a while," said a trader for a trust bank's securities unit.
Investors' buying on dips also likely to provide support, but caution ahead of a three-day weekend and a 10-year JGB auction next week is likely to cap the upside, he said.

JGBs will probably test the upside early, after ending on a firm note at 125.22 on LIFFE overnight, but will recede later in the day as position adjustment sets in, the trader for a trust bank's securities unit said.
Traders said the Finance Ministry is expected to hold an auction for 10-year JGBs next Wednesday.
Investors are unlikely to move too aggressively ahead of the auction, a brokerage house trader said.
The coupon rate for the new 10-year issue is likely to be set at 2.5 percent rather than 2.6 percent, judging from current market conditions, the first trader said.

The BOJ's wholesale price index (WPI) for the first 10 days of July, due at 8.50 a.m. (2350 GMT Thursday), is unlikely to have much impact, as the market is not too concerned about price movements right now, the first trader said.
WPI for the first 10 days of July is expected to have risen by about two percent from a year earlier, the trader said.
The Tokyo JGB market will be closed on Monday for a national holiday. Trading will resume on Tuesday.
